context: Extend the existing Windows antipattern scanner or add a focused AST check, cover aliases and keyword/positional calls, wire it into CI lint, and preserve legitimate binary open calls.
description: PR #1352 fixed the two known bare product read_text calls, and current benchbox has none. The original follow-up also required a durable ratchet so locale-default reads cannot return. Add an AST-based check over benchbox for Path.read_text/open text reads without explicit encoding, with an allowlist only for intentionally binary or locale-sensitive boundaries.

preserves.behavior: Binary file opens and explicit non-UTF8 encodings remain allowed.
The explicit UTF-8 product fixes from PR #1352 remain unchanged.

verifications.expected: fails to reject a bare product read_text call on the unfixed tree; exit 0 after ratchet

work_units.evidence: Inventoried 30 benchbox read_text calls: all explicitly encode today; call forms include keyword/positional encodings, explicit errors policy, and unrelated binary reads. Existing scanner covered only executable bits and Unix signals.
work_units.summary: Inventory product text-read call forms and existing scanner coverage

work_units.evidence: WA003 AST rule rejects missing/None/ambiguous encoding and preserves positional, keyword, computed, non-UTF8, and binary reads; 30 focused tests pass.
work_units.summary: Add AST detection and positive/negative fixtures

work_units.evidence: windows-antipatterns-check runs from make lint, report-all ci-lint, and required code-lint guard; 17 parity/marker tests pass and product scan covers 977 files cleanly.
work_units.summary: Wire the ratchet into local and required CI lint
